subject.title: fix(memory-core): guard catch-block async calls and supplement search against unhandled rejections

question: Should memory_search corpus=all skip failed supplements when at least one sibling succeeds while returning unavailable when every registered supplement fails?
rationale: That choice fixes sibling-result loss but changes the visible retrieval contract, and related open PRs already propose different total-failure semantics.

options.title: Accept degraded partial results
options.body: Require redacted real runtime proof, then land this direction if maintainers want healthy supplement results to survive broken siblings while total supplement outage is reported unavailable.

options.title: Preserve graceful total-failure degradation
options.body: Ask for a revision that keeps fulfilled results and treats all-failed supplements as empty or warning-only if that is the desired compatibility contract.

options.title: Consolidate with older candidates
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers prefer the narrower Promise.allSettled or named-offender logging approach from the existing open candidate PRs.

recommendation.title: Accept degraded partial results
recommendation.body: Require redacted real runtime proof, then land this direction if maintainers want healthy supplement results to survive broken siblings while total supplement outage is reported unavailable.

likelyOwner.reason: The current helper blame, recent refactor ownership, and merged adjacent repair metadata make vincentkoc the best available owner for the failure-contract choice.
